title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 5c (third column, intact = black traces) and legend; Supplementary Table 5 rows for Extended Data Fig. 5c
quote: DNa01 has monosynaptic connections to 25 other DNs and triggers in place turning.
mapping_basis: Paper name DNa01 is a MANC type name, but synonyms.csv also lists DNa01 as an (ambiguous) hemibrain name of DNxl022 and driver_lines.csv lists SS00731 as AMBIGUOUS DNa01;DNxl022 with preferred DNa01; chose DNa01 (Namiki line identity).
stimulation: 640 nm laser aimed at neck/thorax, 21 uW; 10 trials per fly, 25 s between trials
sensory_condition: tethered on air-suspended spherical treadmill; fly holder filled with saline; protocol intended to reduce spontaneous movement
coordination_notes: described only as 'in place turning'; legs not tracked
notes: Turn velocity rises to roughly 400 deg/s during stimulation vs a small rise in no-DN controls (intact DNa01 vs headless P = 0.003, Supplementary Table 5). Pre-stimulus state was not restricted to walking or resting, and legs were neither tracked nor described, so whether the sustained ball rotation reflects >=3 stepping cycles per leg pair cannot be read from the paper; coded unclear for all pairs. Paper does not state expression pattern or off-target labelling of SS00731 (kit row from Namiki 2018 lists ~5 unnamed background off-target cell types), so line_specificity = unknown.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 5c (third column, headless = blue traces) and legend; Supplementary Table 5 rows 'DNa01 v. control, headless/headless'
quote: triggers in place turning. This is quantified as an increase in turn velocity. This behavior is lost in headless animals.
mapping_basis: Paper name DNa01 is a MANC type name, but synonyms.csv also lists DNa01 as an (ambiguous) hemibrain name of DNxl022 and driver_lines.csv lists SS00731 as AMBIGUOUS DNa01;DNxl022 with preferred DNa01; chose DNa01 (Namiki line identity).
stimulation: 640 nm laser aimed at neck/thorax, 21 uW; 10 trials per fly, 25 s between trials
sensory_condition: decapitated, neck stump sealed with UV glue, >=10 min recovery; tethered on spherical treadmill
n_flies_note: 6 headless DNa01 flies x 10 trials; 5 headless control flies
notes: Headless turn velocity (P = 0.206) and side velocity (P = 0.392) do not differ from headless controls (Supplementary Table 5). 'no_visible_effect' refers only to these measured ball parameters. Forward velocity is not shown for DNa01 and no leg movement is described in text, legend or Supplementary Discussion ('their activation alone (i.e., in headless animals) is not sufficient to drive turning'); headless flies were retained only if legs showed spontaneous coordinated movement. Loss of turning therefore does not establish absence of rhythmic stepping, so legs are unclear rather than no. Supplementary Video 4 Part 3 also shows DNa01 headless flies hanging without ground contact, but videos were not downloaded and no text reports that condition, so no record.
